sections.content:
Interesting! After moving the tip LEFT 5 times and then clicking the white block at (50, 30), the block turned GREEN (NNN) instead of the usual cycle. The grid now shows:
```
g N g
W g W
g W g
```
So the top-middle white block is now green. The tip position on the bar seems to affect what color gets painted!
Looking at the upper bar, the tip is now near the left end (over the blue/sky-blue section). When I clicked with the tip in this position, the white block turned green.
Previously, when the tip was on the right side (over gray), clicking white blocks also turned them green. So the tip position might not matter for white blocks, but let me test further.
Let me check: when the tip is on the left (blue section), what happens when I click a gray block? Does it turn green or blue or something else?
Actually wait, let me look more carefully. The grid shows:
```
g N g  (row 49-51: corners gray, center green)
W g W  (row 54-56: left white, center gray, right white)
g W g  (row 59-61: corners gray, center white)
```
So only the top-middle block changed from white to green. The other white blocks remain white. This is consistent with clicking that one block.
Let me now test: with the tip on the left side, click a gray block to see if it turns a different color.
